summary: Collett Cox is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. She earned her PhD at Columbia University under Alex Wayman and Yoshito S. Hakeda, and studied at Tokyo and Ryukoku universities. She long served as professor at the University of Washington.
Congjun Long works in computational linguistics and Tibetology. Long has held posts at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences and the Institute of Software at the Chinese Academy of Sciences.
Conor Roddy specializes in philosophy and Indology. He earned a PhD from the University of Texas at Austin, attested in 2011, under the supervision of Kathleen Higgins.

Conrad Bursian (1830–1883) was a scholar of history and archaeology. Educated at Leipzig and Berlin, he held posts at Leipzig (~1856–1858), Tübingen (~1861–1864), Zurich (~1864–1869), Jena (~1869–1874), and Munich (~1874–1883).
Conrad M. Arensberg (1910–1997) studied at Harvard University (~1927–1934). He spent his academic career at Columbia University, holding a post there from around 1946 to 1979.

Constance E. Kassor specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She earned a BA at Smith College and a PhD at Emory University under John D. Dunne and Sara L. McClintock, later joining the Smith College faculty (attested 2014).
Constance Powell Chin specializes in history, archaeology, and religious studies. She studied under Christian Luczanits and earned a master's degree at San Jose State University in 2012.

Constantin Régamey (1907–1982) was an Indologist, Tibetologist, and linguist. Educated at Warsaw and Paris, he lectured at Warsaw (1936) before serving as professor of Slavic and Oriental languages and cultures at the University of Lausanne (1949–1957).

Corinna May Lhoir works in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. Attested in 2026, she is a PhD student at Ghent University and a doctoral researcher, lecturer, and yoga studies programme coordinator at the University of Hamburg.

Corneille Jest (1930–2019) was a scholar of Tibetology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Paris Descartes University, studied under André Leroi-Gourhan in 1972, and held a research post at the CNRS from around 1958 to 1995.
Cornelis Jan Kuiken is a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies. Supervised by Timothy Hugh Barrett and Jan N. Bremmer, he earned his PhD from the University of Groningen in 2002.

Cornelis Petrus Tiele (1830–1902) was a religious studies scholar educated at Amsterdam and the Remonstrant Seminary. He was a professor at the Remonstrant Seminary (1873) and served as professor of the history of religions at Leiden University (1877–1901).
Corrado Pensa is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied under Giuseppe Tucci and Raniero Gnoli, and held a professorship at Sapienza University of Rome (attested 1971).
Cortland Dahl works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teacher Yongey Mingyur Rinpoche and received mentorship from Sarah Harding, Anne Helm, and Erik Pema Kunsang.

Courtney Bruntz works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. She held a professorship at the Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 2015) and serves as professor of East Asian Buddhism at the Numata Center (attested 2026).

Craig Jamieson is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He has been affiliated with the University of Cambridge as a fellow at Queens' College and as curator of the South Asia manuscript collection (attested 2012).
Craig Preston is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Virginia, where he was taught by Jeffrey Hopkins (1980–1981) and Joe Bransford Wilson.

Cristina Pecchia specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. She earned her PhD from Sapienza University of Rome (~1999–2003), researched at the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia, and lectures at the University of Vienna.

Cristina Scherrer-Schaub (born 1947) specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. She served as a professor at the University of Lausanne (~2000–2012) and at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~2001–2016).

Csaba Dezső (born 1973) is an Indologist who earned master's degrees from Eötvös Loránd University and a PhD from Oxford (1998–2004) under Alexis Sanderson. Around 2004, he became an assistant lecturer at Eötvös Loránd University.
